best_for: People with several IMAP or Gmail accounts who want one unified desktop inbox on Mac, Windows or Linux, and who do not need Exchange or a full calendar.
description:
Mailspring is a desktop email app from Foundry 376, LLC, released as open source under the GPL-3.0 license. It works with Gmail, iCloud, Office 365, Outlook.com, Yahoo, FastMail and any IMAP/SMTP provider.

Sent something too soon? Click Undo and the message goes back to your Drafts folder. When an invitation arrives by email, you can see the event details and RSVP right in the message. The composer checks grammar with LanguageTool, and you can set a follow-up reminder that brings a thread back to your inbox if nobody replies. The app runs in dozens of languages, with a right-to-left layout for Hebrew and Arabic, and fits into each desktop: taskbar badges and jump lists on Windows, the system tray and Wayland on Linux.

points.title: The basics are free and unlimited
points.text: Unlimited accounts, the unified inbox, search, mail rules, signatures, templates, themes and spellcheck cost nothing and work without signing up for anything.

points.title: Extras come in weekly rations
points.text: With a free Mailspring ID you get small weekly allowances of Pro features: 15 snoozes, 5 send-later messages, 5 read receipts and 5 tracked links, among others. When one runs out it comes back the next week.

points.title: Pro is USD 8 a month
points.text: Pro costs USD 8 per month or USD 85 per year and makes most of those features unlimited. Translation stays capped at 800 messages a week and profile lookups at 20. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: No Exchange, no POP3
points.text: Mailspring speaks IMAP, plus Microsoft 365 through OAuth. Exchange Web Services, ActiveSync and POP3 are not supported, and the calendar is only a read-only preview for Google accounts.

points.title: Scheduled mail needs the app open
points.text: Send-later messages go out from your computer, so Mailspring must be running at the time. Your mail and passwords stay on your machine; the account service only stores metadata such as snooze and reminder data.

points.title: Open source, verified Flatpak
points.text: Both the app and its C++ sync engine are GPLv3 on GitHub. The Flathub package for x64 and Arm64 is verified as published by Mailspring.

points.title: Downgrades mostly on Windows
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 38 versions, with a per-user installer. macOS (13 or later) and Linux list only the current release, so going back there needs another source.
